figures.caption: Fig 2. Time evolution of the Li (100) | LPSC (100) interface over a 20 ns MD simulation. Initially, the PS₄ units of LPSC near the interface decompose to form an amorphous interphase (highlighted in blue box), which gradually evolves into a crystalline region (highlighted in red box) after approximately 11 ns. Atomic species are color-coded: Li (purple), S (yellow), P (blue), and Cl (green)

figures.caption: Fig 3. (a) Time evolution of PS₄ decomposition in the LPSC region over 20 ns, showing a plateau following SEI formation. (b) Atomic structure of the interfacial crystalline SEI region compared with the (100), (010), and (001) surface orientations of bulk Li₂S, revealing structural alignment. (c) Radial distribution functions (RDFs) of the bulk Li₂S and the interfacial crystalline region, (d) Mean squared displacement (MSD) of Li ions in the remaining LPSC bulk and the SEI region.
figures.src: 3. Deciphering Li₂S-like SEI Formation Mechanism at LiArgyrodite Anodic Interfaces via Large-Scale Machine-Learned Reactive Dynamics.pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 4. Time-resolved evolution of S and Li migration and Li₂S formation at the Li | LPSC interface. (a-b) Z-position vs. time heatmaps showing the spatial distribution of (a) S and (b) Li atoms during the simulation. The decomposition of PS₄ units releases S atoms that migrate toward the Li-rich region, while Li simultaneously diffuses from the Li metal side, leading to the formation of an interfacial SEI layer. (c) Representative atomic configurations at selected time steps (1, 7, 11, 12, and 20 ns) illustrate the sequential process of sulfur accumulation (①), Li infiltration (②), and nucleation and growth of crystalline Li₂S (③).

figures.caption: Fig. 5. Comparison of SEI formation and PS₄ decomposition at the Li (100) | the LPSC (100) interface with and without a sulfur coating over 50 ns of MD simulation. (a) Initial uncoated structure consisting of 20 nm the LPSC and 16 nm Li metal. (b) Initial configuration with an additional sulfur coating (~3 nm) inserted between the LPSC and Li layers. Final interfacial structures after 50 ns MD simulation for (c) the uncoated and (d) sulfur-coated systems, showing differences in SEI thickness and crystallinity. (e) Time evolution of the number of intact PS₄ units in the LPSC region, highlighting suppressed decomposition in the sulfur-coated system.
